units.title: Unit 59 — Liking and disliking
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 122–123 (PDF pages 126–127).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
learningObjectives: Describe degrees of liking, love, respect and enjoyment using common noun and adjective pairings.
Express dislikes, aversions and negative reactions with appropriate collocations and prepositions.
State preferences, express enthusiasm and distinguish pleasure, pride, offence and sympathy.
Choose a suitable tone and register for strong positive and negative feelings.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: My sister has a particular liking for quiet cafés.
items.note: Use a particular liking for to describe a specific, often personal preference.

items.pt: um gosto verdadeiro por; uma simpatia sincera por
items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: He developed a genuine liking for his new neighbours.
items.note: Genuine stresses that the positive feeling is sincere, not merely polite.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: A great love of wildlife inspired her to study ecology.
items.note: The noun love often takes of when describing a long-standing interest.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: A passionate love of jazz inspired him to become a musician.
items.note: Passionate adds emotional intensity to love of something.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: The team has the greatest regard for its former coach.
items.note: Regard is relatively formal here and expresses respect rather than simply liking.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: I have the highest regard for her judgement.
items.note: A formal phrase for deep respect; often used in professional contexts.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: The sheer enjoyment of solving the puzzle kept him busy all evening.
items.note: Sheer highlights enjoyment for its own sake, without another reward.

items.pt: sentir grande prazer com; aproveitar muito
items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: Many people get great enjoyment out of growing their own vegetables.
items.note: The pattern is get enjoyment out of followed by a noun or -ing form.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: It was a great pleasure to meet the new members of the team.
items.note: Common in polite greetings and acknowledgements, including formal contexts.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: It was a huge pleasure to see everyone together again.
items.note: Huge is an emphatic, slightly more expressive modifier of pleasure.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: Several students express a clear preference for online lessons.
items.note: Express a preference for something, often when asked to choose between alternatives.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: Our customers have a strong preference for local suppliers.
items.note: Preference normally takes for when identifying the preferred option.

items.pt: uma aversão intensa a; um forte desgosto por
items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: She has an intense dislike of crowded lifts.
items.note: Intense strengthens dislike and conveys a powerful negative feeling.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: Some people take an instant dislike to new colleagues before getting to know them.
items.note: This means to start disliking a person or thing immediately; use to, not for.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: He has a huge aversion to unnecessary risk.
items.note: Aversion to describes strong reluctance or dislike; it can take an -ing form.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: She has a strong aversion to being interrupted.
items.note: Use aversion to, not aversion for, even before an -ing clause.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: The novel explores a deep hatred of injustice.
items.note: Deep hatred describes a very strong negative emotion, more intense than dislike.

items.section: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
items.example: Deep-rooted hatred between the groups made talks difficult.
items.note: Deep-rooted indicates that the hostility has existed for a long time.

items.example: Please state your preference for a morning or afternoon appointment.
items.note: State a preference is relatively formal and common on forms or in requests.

items.example: The festival tries to cater for everyone's tastes with a wide range of activities.
items.note: British English cater for means provide options suitable for different people; cater to is also common.

items.example: Our engineers take pride in producing reliable equipment.
items.note: Use take pride in followed by a noun or -ing form.

items.pt: não gostar nem um pouco da ideia de; não ficar animado com a perspectiva de
items.example: I do not relish the thought of explaining the delay to our customers.
items.note: A negative expression for anticipating something unpleasant; relish the thought of is usually negated.

items.example: They take pleasure in helping new colleagues settle in.
items.note: Pleasure in normally precedes a noun or -ing form.

items.example: Some guests take offence at jokes about their accent.
items.note: Take offence at means react negatively because something seems insulting.

items.pt: não ter nenhuma compaixão por; não se solidarizar com
items.example: I have no sympathy for anyone who cheats customers.
items.note: Sympathy here means understanding or compassion, not simply approval.

items.example: The new manager received a warm welcome from the whole team.
items.note: Warm describes friendly and enthusiastic treatment upon arrival.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: That song is an absolute favourite at family parties.
items.note: Absolute strengthens favourite; it is not an adjective for physical size.

items.pt: um favorito de todos os tempos
items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: This film remains an all-time favourite of mine.
items.note: All-time favourite describes a lasting preference across many years.

items.pt: um grande apreciador de; alguém que adora
items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: My grandfather is a great lover of classical music.
items.note: Here lover means an enthusiastic admirer, not a romantic partner.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: She's an ardent fan of the local football club.
items.note: Ardent indicates strong, often openly expressed enthusiasm.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: He is a dedicated fan of the author and owns every book.
items.note: Dedicated suggests loyal, sustained interest.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: I am a keen admirer of her scientific work.
items.note: Keen emphasises enthusiastic admiration and is common in British English.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: The way she handled the emergency continues to fill me with admiration.
items.note: The structure is fill someone with admiration; the pronoun changes with the speaker.

items.section: C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes
items.example: It continues to give me pleasure to see my students succeed.
items.note: The pattern give someone pleasure expresses enjoyment or satisfaction.

items.example: I feel great love for the relatives who helped raise me.
items.note: Love for normally introduces the person or thing receiving affection.

items.example: I get more pleasure from walking in the countryside than shopping.
items.note: Use from to identify the activity that provides enjoyment.

items.pt: optar por um assento no corredor
items.example: On long flights, I usually go for an aisle seat.
items.note: Go for is informal and means choose or prefer an option.

sectionsChecked: A · Strong statements: nouns and adjectives
B · Verbs and nouns: examples concerning service and preferences
C · Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes

units.title: Unit 60 — Praising and criticising
units.source: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition); printed pages 124–125 (PDF pages 128–129).
units.bookTitle: English Collocations in Use — Intermediate (2nd Edition)
units.category: Functions · praise, approval, criticism and condemnation
learningObjectives: Give praise and congratulations and describe positive audience or critical reception.
Distinguish giving credit, taking credit, approving of something and expressing admiration.
Describe criticism, disapproval, condemnation and objection with appropriate intensity and register.
Use idiomatic and formal expressions for public commendation and strong criticism.

items.pt: ter apenas elogios para; só ter elogios a fazer a
items.example: I have nothing but praise for the nurses who cared for him.
items.note: An emphatic expression meaning there is no criticism to offer.

items.example: I would like to offer my congratulations to the winning team.
items.note: Offer congratulations to a person; congratulate a person on an achievement.

items.example: The dancers received thunderous applause after the final scene.
items.note: Thunderous describes very loud, enthusiastic applause.

items.example: Her promotion was richly deserved after years of excellent work.
items.note: Richly deserved means fully deserved and strongly approves of the outcome.

items.example: The students managed to put on a dazzling production with a small budget.
items.note: Put on means stage or present a show; dazzling describes impressive quality.

items.pt: uma apresentação excepcional; um desempenho extraordinário
items.example: The violinist gave an outstanding performance on opening night.
items.note: Outstanding conveys exceptionally high quality in sport, the arts or work.

items.pt: levar todo o mérito por; assumir todo o crédito por
items.example: The director refused to take full credit for the team's success.
items.note: Take credit for means claim recognition; full stresses sole or complete credit.

items.example: We warmly congratulate everyone who completed the course.
items.note: Warmly describes genuine enthusiasm, not physical warmth.

items.example: The small-budget film went on to receive critical acclaim.
items.note: Critical here refers to professional reviewers, not negative criticism.

items.example: The volunteers justly deserve recognition for their efforts.
items.note: Justly means with good reason or fairness and emphasises that praise is warranted.

items.example: The new play received rave reviews in the local press.
items.note: Rave reviews are extremely positive, not merely numerous reviews.

items.pt: atribuir mérito a; dar crédito a
items.example: The researcher was careful to give credit to her colleagues.
items.note: Give credit to acknowledges someone's contribution; contrast take credit for.

items.pt: receber elogios por; conquistar reconhecimento por
items.example: The design team may win praise for its energy-saving solution.
items.note: Win praise for connects positive recognition to a particular achievement.

items.example: The retiring conductor was delighted to receive a standing ovation.
items.note: A standing ovation happens when an audience rises to applaud.

items.pt: admirar muito; ter enorme consideração por
items.example: Her students think the world of their teacher.
items.note: An informal expression of very strong affection or admiration.

items.pt: tecer elogios a ela; elogiar muito alguém
items.example: Her former colleagues still sing her praises years later.
items.note: The idiom sing someone's praises means speak enthusiastically about them; the pronoun can change.

items.example: Clients often speak highly of the support staff.
items.note: Speak highly of is a conventional way to express favourable opinions.

items.example: Even his competitors speak well of his professionalism.
items.note: Speak well of is positive but may be less emphatic than speak highly of.

items.example: Her family warmly approve of her decision to study abroad.
items.note: Warmly marks wholehearted approval; approve of can take a noun or -ing form.

items.example: I heartily approve of measures that make cycling safer.
items.note: Heartily intensifies approve of and expresses strong support.

items.pt: dar sua bênção a; dar sua aprovação a
items.example: Will you give your blessing to the new community project?
items.note: Figurative blessing means approval or goodwill, not necessarily a religious act.

items.pt: dar uma grande salva de palmas
items.example: Let's give a big clap to the young performers.
items.note: A friendly and informal invitation to applaud someone.

items.example: Please give a round of applause to our guest speaker.
items.note: A standard public-speaking formula for inviting audience applause.

items.pt: um reconhecimento; um tapinha nas costas em sinal de elogio
items.example: The team deserves a pat on the back for meeting the deadline.
items.note: Often figurative: recognition or praise for a job well done.

items.example: The proposal is likely to come in for criticism from residents.
items.note: Come in for criticism means receive it; often used in reports or news.

items.example: The company promised to respond to criticism with clear evidence.
items.note: Responding to criticism does not necessarily mean agreeing with it.

items.example: The minister tried to counter criticism with evidence of earlier reforms.
items.note: Counter criticism means argue back against criticism rather than accept it.

items.example: The developer chose to dismiss criticism of the new design.
items.note: Dismiss suggests treating objections as unimportant or unfounded.

items.example: Several parents began to show disapproval during the meeting.
items.note: Show disapproval describes an observable negative reaction.

items.example: Employees may express disapproval of the changes without being rude.
items.note: Express disapproval is more formal and direct than a displeased look.

items.example: She gave him a look of disapproval when he interrupted.
items.note: A non-verbal expression; the usual pattern is a look of disapproval.

items.example: His suggestion was met with a frown of disapproval.
items.note: A frown is a facial expression showing concern, anger or disapproval.

items.example: The initial plans attracted harsh criticism from local groups.
items.note: Harsh emphasises severity and may imply a lack of kindness.

items.example: Constant criticism made it difficult for the new employee to feel confident.
items.note: Constant means repeated or continuing; it says nothing about whether criticism is fair.

items.example: Good mentors offer constructive criticism alongside encouragement.
items.note: Constructive criticism aims to help someone improve rather than merely condemn.

items.example: Several experts were highly critical of the safety proposal.
items.note: Highly intensifies critical; use critical of, not critical about, as the normal pattern here.

items.example: The report was sharply critical of the agency's delays.
items.note: Sharply conveys pointed or severe criticism, often in formal writing.

items.example: Local groups roundly criticise the new parking rules.
items.note: Roundly means strongly or thoroughly; it does not mean briefly or politely.

items.pt: criticar ferozmente; atacar com duras críticas
items.example: Opposition groups fiercely criticise the proposed restrictions.
items.note: Fiercely emphasises intensity and determination in criticism.

items.example: Residents bitterly criticise the failure to repair their homes.
items.note: Bitterly often conveys anger or resentment as well as force.

items.example: She is a harsh critic of any policy that weakens public services.
items.note: A harsh critic expresses severe negative judgement.

items.pt: um crítico contundente; alguém que critica abertamente
items.example: He is an outspoken critic of the company's environmental record.
items.note: Outspoken means willing to voice strong opinions directly and publicly.

items.example: I strongly disapprove of hiding important information from customers.
items.note: Use disapprove of plus a noun or -ing form; strongly marks firm opposition.

items.example: My parents thoroughly disapprove of reckless driving.
items.note: Thoroughly intensifies disapprove of and means completely.

items.example: Community leaders severely condemn attacks on journalists.
items.note: Severely marks strong moral or official denunciation.

items.example: The decision faced wholesale condemnation from several professional bodies.
items.note: Wholesale emphasises very extensive condemnation; it is relatively formal.

items.example: The act of violence met with universal condemnation across the community.
items.note: Universal means virtually everyone disapproved; not literally every individual.

items.example: Many residents strongly object to the removal of the trees.
items.note: Object to takes a noun or an -ing form, not a bare infinitive.

items.pt: opor-se veementemente a; contestar com firmeza
items.example: Local businesses strenuously object to the proposed parking charges.
items.note: Strenuously expresses determined and forceful opposition.

items.example: The student project could win a lot of praise for its creativity.
items.note: The phrase highlights the amount of positive recognition earned.

items.example: We would like to offer warm congratulations to everyone involved.
items.note: Warm congratulations is a positive, friendly formula for celebrating success.

sectionsChecked: A · Praising: review text, applause, credit, congratulation and approval
B · Criticising: disapproval, criticism, condemnation, objection and intensifiers
